name: reduce_sum
summary: Keep-lastdim ReduceSum only: dY[..., N] (contig) -> out[N] by summing across flattened leading dims M. Axis is treated as a contract flag: axis==0 required. Variants: f32->f32, f16->f32, f16->f16. F16 paths have half2(vec2) fastpath when N even and pointers 4B aligned.
contract: - Input: dY with rank>=2, contiguous, shape [..., N]
- Output: out with rank==1, contiguous, shape [N]
- Reduction: out[j] = sum_{i in [0..M-1]} dY_flat[i, j], where M = product(shape[:-1])
- axis must be 0 (current lowering emits axis=0 for this keep_lastdim kernel-id).
- axis is NOT a general reduction axis here; other axes are unsupported by this kernel-id.
- dY.contiguous must be true (assumes row-major flatten => stride-last == 1 implicitly)
abi: - get_axis_default0(): accepts schema_id==0 or RSUM; otherwise returns 0
- if attr missing or invalid => axis=0
- this op is intentionally specialized; axis!=0 is rejected by supported()/check()
notes: Implementation reduces each output column with one CUDA block; no atomics.
Threadblock reduction is warp-shuffle + shared warp-sums (block_sum<256>).
Launch shape: grid.x = N (or N/2 for half2), block.x = 256.
INT_MAX guards: if M or N exceeds INT_MAX => NotImplemented.

experiments.title: No-atomic per-column block reduction
experiments.change: One block per output column; reduce across rows via block_sum().
experiments.why: Avoid atomicAdd contention on out[N] when M is large.
experiments.hypothesis: Better scaling when M large, N moderate; predictable determinism.
experiments.next: Consider 2D tiling (multiple cols per block) when N is huge to reduce grid.x launch overhead.

experiments.title: half2 pack over columns
experiments.change: For f16, process two columns per blockIdx.x using __half2 loads.
experiments.why: Halve grid.x and use vectorized loads; improve memory efficiency.
experiments.hypothesis: Higher throughput for even N with aligned pointers.
experiments.next: Try accumulation in float2 with vectorized LDG (ld.global.v2) and unroll over rows.

experiments.title: Axis freeze to axis==0 in AttrBlob
experiments.change: Treat axis as contract flag (must be 0) instead of dynamic reduction axis.
experiments.why: Keep kernel-id semantics stable and simplify lowering/dispatcher.
experiments.next: Add separate kernel-id for generic axis reduction if needed later.

measurements.notes: Report effective read/write bytes: reads=M*N*2B, writes=N*4B (f16->f32). Compare scalar vs half2.
